additions: ExoFOP policy changed on 2026-08-19: community candidates from TESS, Kepler, K2 'and beyond' are accepted again, but only after publication in a peer-reviewed journal (or an RNAAS that cites a previously published detection+vetting methodology), with upload approval requested via the 'Published Candidate Upload Request' form; names are TID.nn (TIC ID), a 'discovery data source' field distinguishes cTOIs (TESS) from 'Other Discovery Data Source' candidates, and >=2 of period/epoch/depth (all four incl. duration for cTOI consideration) plus supporting plots and a TOI/candidate cross-check are required (exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/candidate_help.php). Practical consequence: the realistic end state for ANY solo candidate is 'refereed paper first, ExoFOP listing second'; the brief's 'CTOI -> TOI' path for a Rabtsevich-type star is no longer an unreviewed upload.

TESS-SPOC FFI target selection (Caldwell et al. 2020, ar5iv 2011.05495; MAST HLSP page): (1) all 2-min targets; (2) 'include' targets with H<=10 OR distance<=100 pc, crowding>=0.5 and T<=16; (3) field stars in T order with T<=13.5, logg>=3.5, crowding>=0.8; cap 10,000 per CCD (152,359-160,000 per sector). SPOC has run TPS on FFI targets since May 2021 (single-sector DV products from Sector 36, multi-sector from Sector 56; no multi-sector search of Prime/EM1 FFI data). Therefore every GCNS M dwarf within 100 pc with T<=16 and crowding>=0.5 is nominally a SPOC-searched star; novelty checks must include TESS-SPOC DV/TCE products on MAST, not only TOIs. The real gaps are: d>100 pc faint stars, crowding<0.5 stars, cap-dropped stars in dense fields, and periods needing multi-sector coverage in Sectors 1-55.

TARS (TESS All-Sky Rotation Survey; Boyle, Bouma & Mann; DOI 10.17909/2sff-fn29) is a ready-made HLSP of CPM-corrected FFI light curves for ~7.5 million TIC stars with T<16 and parallax>2 mas (d<500 pc), Sectors 1-96, 0.14 MB per star-sector, FFI cadence (200 s in S81). It covers KIC 5689121 (TESSMAG 15.21) in all 10 of Kuber's sectors; measured 1-h noise 5,029 ppm in S81 (Stassun model ~5,900 ppm). For a faint-M-dwarf TESS search this removes the TESScut/TGLC extraction cost, with the caveat that the causal-pixel-model detrending was tuned for rotation periods 0.1-20 d and must be injection-tested for transit preservation.

QLP (T<13.5 for EM1 Years 1-2 per Kunimoto et al. 2021/2022 HLSP notes) 'also produces light curves for select fainter M dwarfs' from Sector 41 onward; and the TESS Faint-star Search (Kunimoto et al. 2022, ApJS 259, 33) vetted 10.5<T<13.5 QLP signals (1,617 TOIs, Sectors 1-26). Current QLP faint limits for EM2/EM3 remain unverified (no published note found).

A flux-based contamination pre-filter for KBONUS light curves, measured here: the Kepler zero point Kp + 2.5 log10(median FLUX e/s) = 25.31 +/- 0.20 (10 files with valid KEPMAG). For an uncontaminated M dwarf G - Kp_implied is within +/-0.2 (KIC 5689121: -0.03). The two anomalously quiet stars have G - Kp_implied = +2.26 (KIC 10198500) and +2.30 (KIC 8565344): their PSF flux is ~8x too bright, i.e. the originating target's light; two more are 2.3x too bright. Flag any file with G - Kp_implied > 0.5 (also: missing KEPMAG = 1e+20 in the header is itself a warning) before searching.

The Kepler known/model realism ratio is magnitude dependent: 0.45 for Kp<16 (114 known vs 255.6 model) and 0.15 for Kp>16 (15 vs 100.4). For a pool with median G 18.5 the appropriate discount is ~0.15, giving ~15-20 expected planets in Kuber's 1,836 stars rather than ~40, which narrows the gap to his harvest of 1 candidate + ~5 unresolved leads.

Astrophysical false-positive rates are missing from the brief: Fressin et al. 2013 (arXiv:1301.0842) find a global Kepler FP rate of 9.4%, 12.3% for Earth-size (0.8-1.25 Re), 6.7% for small Neptunes (2-4 Re), 17.7% for giants (6-22 Re). These are for Kepler primary targets dominating their apertures; for KBONUS background sources extracted from a brighter neighbour's TPF the blended-EB/contaminant probability is much higher (TRICERATOPS FPP 0.069 for KIC 5689121 is the concrete example), so any yield model should carry an FP fraction of >=10% and a per-candidate FPP calculation, not just detection completeness.

DC15 Table 5 also gives a 0.5-1.0 Re row (51.4% per star at P<50 d, 59.7% at P<200 d); the brief restricts to 1-4 Re. In Kepler/KBONUS data at Kp<15 the minimum detectable radius is 0.4-0.7 Re, so sub-Earths contribute ~25 extra transiting planets per 1000 M dwarfs in the bright bins (with only 36-54% injection recovery in DC15's own cells).

Exoplanet Archive TAP table names verified on 2026-10-17 (TAP_SCHEMA.tables): cumulative, Q1_Q17_DR25_KOI, Q1_Q17_DR25_TCE, Q1_Q17_DR25_SUP_KOI, Q1_Q17_DR25_KS, Q1_Q17_DR25_SUP_KS, KEPLERSTELLAR, K2TARGETS, k2pandc, k2names, toi, ps, pscomppars, stellarhosts. There is no TAP table for the Kepler certified-false-positive or FPP tables (web interface only). q1_q17_dr25_stellar does not exist; use Q1_Q17_DR25_KS.

For M dwarfs T - G is about -1.0 to -1.1 (TIC 120686465: T 15.21, G 16.28), so convert GCNS G to Tmag with T ~ G - 1.0; the brief's G - 0.7 undercounts the T<15 pool by ~10% (G<16 within 100 pc = 131,614).

tess-point (pip install tess-point; tess_stars2px.py) is the standard way to replace the 2/4/8-sector scenario with a measured sector-count histogram for a target list; it is not installed in the sandbox (unverified here, but it is the tool the TESS GI office distributes).

Kuber's 'first screen' BLS SNR is not Kepler's MES: Kepler's 7.1-sigma MES threshold and DR25 completeness curves refer to the TPS matched-filter statistic on whitened data, while astropy BoxLeastSquares objective='snr' uses the supplied dy; red-noise-inflated dy (as in Kuber's 'aperture local SNR 13.7' vs '26.7 BLS SNR') changes the number by 2x. Any yield model or threshold must state which statistic it uses.
remaining_uncertainties: The TESS-SPOC 10,000-per-CCD cap: how many GCNS M dwarfs within 100 pc were actually dropped in crowded sectors is unknown; the HLSP lists the selection rules but not per-sector completeness. A direct check (search TESS-SPOC products for a GCNS subsample via lightkurve author='TESS-SPOC') was not run.

Current QLP magnitude limit in Extended Missions 2-3 (Sectors 56+): only the EM1 notes (T<13.5, plus 'select fainter M dwarfs' from S41) were found; if QLP now reaches T~14-15 the TESS residual shrinks further.
The BLS runtimes and white-noise Monte Carlo were taken from the agent's output file and not re-timed; the sandbox CPUs are shared (+/-30%).

EPIC k2_teff/k2_logg for faint K2 stars are photometric (Huber et al. 2016) and known to misclassify some giants/reddened dwarfs; the 27,666-star K2 cool-dwarf count is an upper bound on genuine M dwarfs, and which of them were already searched end-to-end (Dressing+2017/2019, Hardegree-Ullman+2020, Zink+2021) was not established.

The flux-based contamination test (G - Kp_implied) was calibrated on only 10 files (zero-point scatter 0.2 mag); a scan of all 1,836 eligible stars (~4 h of downloads) is needed before adopting the 0.5-mag threshold.

Whether TARS CPM light curves preserve 2-h transits at full depth was not tested (injection-recovery needed); their 1-h noise for T~15 matched the Stassun model within 15%, but transit-depth fidelity is a separate question.

The physical nature of Kuber's two inverted stars at candidate strength (KIC 8701308, KIC 5283912) remains unexamined; if they would fail his pixel/dilution tests the inverted-null rate at candidate strength overstates the risk for the real candidate.

The realism-factor split (0.45 vs 0.15 by Kp) conflates DR25 pipeline completeness, Robovetter losses, KOI-host Teff crossmatch issues and the use of CDPP medians that hide active stars; it was derived from the agent's model table, not from an independent injection study.
K2 known-planet count differs by parameter row (134 vs 150); the K2 candidate catalogues from Zink et al. 2021 and Kruse et al. 2019 were not merged, so 'already found' in K2 is a lower bound.
ExoFOP's new policy page does not say whether a declined-then-revised RNAAS (Kuber's AAS82222) would qualify; the RNAAS clause requires a cited, previously published methodology paper.
